title: Exact trial-summary constraints permit both pooling outcomes in 115 of 130 selected Allen input groups
abstract: We tested whether exact finite trial constraints resolve a prior pooling ambiguity in Allen cortical response summaries. We applied a known count-dependent mean-median bound to 130 selected same-sign input groups. Exact feasible mean intervals gave four guaranteed sum losses, 11 guaranteed benefits and 115 groups that permit both outcomes under independent-noise linear addition. This adds two benefit certificates to the prior unit-SD relaxation. A continuous trial construction attained both gain extrema with the stored count, median and standard deviation. Across 323 group cases, 1430 marginal trial constructions had scaled moment errors below 4.8e-15. This is a same-data feasibility extension, not an independent biological test. Unknown covariance, empirical-to-population error, fit error and selected slice circuits limit interpretation. Code, aggregate findings, a figure and external regeneration steps support reproduction. External records and fitted witness arrays are not bundled.

display.caption: Exact count constraints add two benefit certificates. Most groups still permit both pooling outcomes in the independent-noise model.
